html:
The Vietnamese general who led the communist forces that beat France at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954, and who commanded North Vietnam's army in the long war with the United States.

Giáp was a history teacher in Hanoi with no military training. He joined the communists in the 1930s and became a close ally of Hồ Chí Minh. In 1944 he formed the first armed unit of the Viet Minh, a few dozen men. By 1954 it was an army of divisions.

In the First Indochina War he learned from costly defeats, then won by patience and logistics: at Điện Biên Phủ his men hauled artillery by hand up the hills around the French base. The victory ended French rule in Indochina.

During the Vietnam War he was defence minister and commander in chief. He is linked with the Tet Offensive of 1968, though his role in planning it is debated. Younger generals led the final campaign that took Saigon in 1975. Giáp lived to 102, revered as one of the great commanders of the 1900s.
sum: The Vietnamese general who led the communist forces that beat France at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954, and who commanded North Vietnam's army in the long war with the United States.
